questions.question: Which of the following is considered the strongest and most secure password?
questions.hint: A strong password uses a mix of uppercase, lowercase, numbers, and special symbols.

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of Two-Factor Authentication (2FA)?
options: To add an extra layer of security beyond just a password
questions.hint: It requires a second piece of evidence to prove your identity.

questions.question: You receive an urgent email from your bank asking you to click a link and 'verify your account details' to avoid account suspension. What is this attack called?
questions.hint: This is a social engineering trick used to 'fish' for your private information.

questions.question: Why is it risky to access sensitive information, like online banking, over a public, unsecured Wi-Fi network?
options: The internet speed is too slow for banking
Attackers can potentially intercept the data sent between your device and the router
Public Wi-Fi automatically deletes your cookies
questions.hint: Unencrypted networks allow others on the same network to potentially 'sniff' your traffic.

questions.question: Under the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR), what does the 'Right to Erasure' (Right to be Forgotten) specifically allow an individual to do?
options: Delete their entire browsing history from their local computer
Request that an organization delete their personal data under certain conditions
Block all emails from a specific sender permanently
Force a search engine to hide all results related to their name
questions.hint: This right focuses on the control a user has over personal data held by third-party companies.
